question.text: A short call (call writer) position has:

answer.text: Maximum profit limited to premium received and theoretically unlimited loss potential
Unlimited profit potential and limited loss
Both profit and loss limited to the premium
Maximum profit equal to the strike price and maximum loss equal to the premium

explanation.text: The Logic: For a short call (call writer), the maximum profit is the premium received, earned when the option expires OTM (S <= X) and is not exercised. The maximum loss is theoretically unlimited because the underlying can rise without bound. The break-even point is Strike + Premium. The Trap: "Unlimited profit potential and limited loss" describes a long call, not a short call. "Both profit and loss limited to the premium" applies to neither side of a call. "Profit equal to strike, loss equal to premium" inverts the writer's payoff entirely. Note: Explanation cleaned to state the expiry condition (option expires OTM, S <= X) and the unlimited-loss / capped-profit structure without malformed fragments.
